issues.description: The template Farm.java declares a helper method singFarmSongVerse without an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/)) whereas the problem statement UML and the solution implementation expect singFarmSongVerse(Animal). This mismatch between the template and the specified design (and solution) can confuse students: they will implement singFarmSong() to iterate animals and call singFarmSongVerse(animal), but the template helper has the wrong signature and will not accept the intended argument.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template helper declaration to match the UML and solution: declare singFarmSongVerse to accept an Animal parameter (private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal)) and update its body to use that animal. Also implement singFarmSong() to iterate over the farm's animals and call singFarmSongVerse(animal). This aligns the template with the specification and the solution while preserving the pedagogical tasks.
